name: Marisol Vega
life: Marisol took a paper route as a kid to pay for punctures. The station has three forms for a bicycle and none asks what it feels like under its rider. She wants the return desk to ask that question before asking for a signature. People around Breakwater Way know Marisol by a small Friday habit. Marisol stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: My first bicycle belonged to three cousins before me. I thought recognizing a color was enough. I called both families from my own desk so neither would have to queue at the station again.
appearance: Marisol is easy to recognize by short black hair swept back and a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow. Usually dressed in a cream pullover with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring, Marisol steadies a cup with both hands while listening when listening.
personality: Marisol treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To give both riders one uninterrupted chance to identify their property.
family: Cory Walker is Marisol’s parent’s cousin. Marisol saves a place. Cory chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The trust with a typo*, Cory says, “I knew the founder when she couldn't afford the exam.”
connections: Hollis Fry. They meet a second time at the property counter to compare what the wrong saddle cost.

reactions.situation: A child's account contradicts the adult at the counter
reactions.response: Marisol lets the child finish describing the bicycle and asks to hear the bell.

reactions.situation: A friend asks for a loan due back before payday
reactions.response: Marisol agrees on a sum and a date with the friend in private, keeping the arrangement out of family gossip.
